<a id="con-01"></a>
## CON-01 - Status labels need readable contrast: tinted background, dark text

White text on saturated status colours often fails contrast; a light tint of the status colour with dark text of the same hue passes.

- **Source:** PDF 21 (printed 20)
- **Applies when:** Status pills, tags, badges, chips.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Contrast helps important things stand out and matters for readability, guidance and accessibility (visual impairments, WCAG).
- Incorrect pills (white text on saturated red/orange/green) have contrast ratios of 2.84:1, 1.81:1 and 1.92:1; corrected pills (light tint with dark coloured text) reach 4.8:1, 4.94:1 and 6.54:1.

**Mistake:** White label text on a mid-saturation status fill.  
**Effect:** Low legibility; fails accessibility guidance.

**Correction:** Use a pale tint of the status colour as background and a dark shade of the same hue as text; verify the ratio.  
**Why it works:** Keeps the colour-coding while restoring luminance contrast.

**Observable checks:**
- Compute text/background contrast for every pill; flag below 4.5:1 for normal-size text (TYP-09).
- Is white text placed on yellow, orange, light green or similar mid-luminance fills?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Source issues / ambiguity:**
- The third ticket is labelled 'Blocked' in green in both versions; likely a source labelling slip. The lesson concerns contrast, not wording.

**Related:** [TYP-09](15-typography.md#typ-09), [COL-04](14-color.md#col-04), [COL-05](14-color.md#col-05)

<a id="con-02"></a>
## CON-02 - Create contrast with colour, weight, size, borders and shadows

Contrast is not only colour: weight/style, size, borders/outlines and shadows also separate and emphasise elements.

- **Source:** PDF 22 (printed 21)
- **Applies when:** When an element needs to stand out from neighbours or its background.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Ways to apply contrast: colour (complementary or analogous, within accessibility guidelines); font weight and style; size for hierarchy; borders and outlines when elements are too similar in colour; shadows to make elements pop and add dimension.

**Mistake:** Relying on a single lever (usually hue) and getting weak differentiation.  
**Effect:** Elements blend together.

**Correction:** Combine levers appropriate to the case, e.g. add an outline when two surfaces share a colour, or a shadow for elevation.  
**Why it works:** Multiple cues are more robust than one.

**Observable checks:**
- When two adjacent surfaces have near-identical colour, is there a border, shadow or spacing that separates them?

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [DEP-01](13-depth.md#dep-01), [DEP-06](13-depth.md#dep-06), [TYP-08](15-typography.md#typ-08), [TYP-11](15-typography.md#typ-11)

*No visual example: the PDF presents this point in text only.*

<a id="con-03"></a>
## CON-03 - Keep text over images legible

Light text that works on a dark photo can fail on a busy or lighter one; use a tonal overlay or a background blur behind the text.

- **Source:** PDF 22 (printed 21)
- **Applies when:** Captions, titles or bylines placed on photos or video.

**What the PDF states** (paraphrased):
- Consider legibility at scale: light text on a dark image may fail on a lighter one.
- Options: an overlay (with layer blur) that complements the image tone, or a background blur.

**Mistake:** White title and byline placed directly on a busy photo.  
**Effect:** Parts of the text become unreadable over light or detailed areas.

**Correction:** Add a gradient/tonal overlay or a blurred band behind the text area.  
**Why it works:** Creates a stable, predictable background for the text regardless of the image.

**Observable checks:**
- Sample contrast at the text's location against the lightest and busiest part of the image behind it.

**Exceptions / limits supported by the source:**
- None stated by the source.

**Related:** [DEP-09](13-depth.md#dep-09), [TYP-09](15-typography.md#typ-09)
